bannedNote.en: Prohibited act under competition rules: squeezing the trunk with crossed legs (scissoring the body) is penalised with hansoku-make. Unlike most banned techniques it has no legitimate contest history to preserve; it is listed so it can be recognised and stopped.

links.title: Do-jime on the IJF technique reference

about.en: Squeezing the opponent's trunk between the legs, ankles crossed around the body. Judo classifies it among the strangles but bans it outright: compressing the trunk this way can injure ribs and organs. Documented for recognition only.

en: Recognise it: legs wrapped around the trunk with the ankles crossed, squeezing
Prohibited in competition and in randori alike
If you feel it applied in practice, tap at once and say so; it should simply not be used

viNotes.en: Recognition only, and worth knowing by feel: the pressure comes around your ribs from legs crossed behind your back, not at a joint or the neck, and it does not build the way a legal technique does. Tap and tell your coach. Nobody should be applying this to anyone.

cue.en: Not a neck strangle at all: the legs cross around the opponent's trunk and squeeze the body.
